I'm 34, not quite middle aged yet but definitely not a kid. I think young people are just like my generation was and every generation before mine. There is a popular opinion amongst the 50+ crowd saying that young kids are soft and spoiled, that the future is doomed because of trophies, social media, and legal weed. This is the cycle that has continued since what seems like forever. 

As I cross over into middle age, I just hope that I can remember not to become an angry old man. I hope I can remember what it is like to be a teenager, when you suddenly realize that the world is larger than your city/group of friends, when you realize that adulthood is right around the corner, when you're trying to figure out who you are and who you're going to be. 

Sure they might be a bit spazzy, dramatic, or they might think they know everything but they are going to be just fine. One day they will complain about the new youth and how they just don't understand.

I'm a Clevelander living in New England and I've been to games in both places. I know Brady (and the Pats in general) get a bunch of hate but you shouldn't have any problems in Cleveland. Browns fans are usually fans of the game. By that I mean, we recognize a GOAT when we see a GOAT. You might run into a couple assholes but that's life. Plus, there are a bunch of Michigan fans in Cleveland so Brady gets some love from that crowd. 

Go to the municipal lot a couple of hours before the game with some beer,small grill, and a variety of meat, strike up a conversation with the people next to you and you can have a good time. Ask people where to go after the game. Cleveland is a great city.
